About Helix AI

Helix AI Inc. was founded in San Francisco in 2021. It trains its own AI models and sells AI agents that do real work inside large companies – answering customers, closing the books and fixing IT tickets. It has about 1,400 people.

Products

Helix Models Large AI models that businesses use through an API.
Helix Agents Ready-made AI agents for customer support, finance and IT.
Helix Studio Tools to build, test and watch over your own agents.

Frequently asked questions

What exactly do I own?

Units in Stockify US Opportunities LLC – Series 14, a Delaware SPV. Its only asset is Helix AI common shares.

What does it cost in total?

3.5% upfront, no yearly fee, and 10% of your profit at exit. On $10,000, fees are $350 and $9,650 is invested.

When can I get my money back?

Only after an IPO or a sale of Helix. After an IPO there is usually a 180-day lock-up. This can take years.

Is expressing interest binding?

No. You only commit when you sign the subscription agreement after your allocation is confirmed on 14 Oct.

How it works

How investing in US private companies works

You invest in US dollars through a Delaware SPV – a small company set up for just one deal. This page explains what you own, what it costs, how long it takes and what can go wrong.

Browse deals Read the risks first
3.5% One-time upfront fee 3.0% placement + 0.5% SPV set-up & admin
$0 Yearly management fee Nothing to pay while you hold
10% Carry, only at exit A share of your profit – none if there’s no profit
1 SPV For every deal Your money sits in escrow, never with Stockify

What you actually own

You own units in an SPV. The SPV owns the company’s shares.
You You sign up, pass the checks for your country and choose how much to invest.
Feeder (UAE & Global) An offshore fund sits in between. It keeps you out of US estate tax. India investors skip this step.
Delaware SPV A US company set up for one deal only. It pools everyone’s money, buys the shares and gives you units.
Company shares The SPV holds the real shares. When the company lists or is sold, the money flows back to you.
Where your money goes: your bank → the deal’s escrow account → used to buy shares when the deal closes. Never to Stockify. If the company blocks the transfer, you get it back.
StockifyExample: Stockify US Opportunities LLC – Series 14 (Helix AI) · Rules confirmed in phase 2

Getting in takes about four weeks. Getting out can take years – plan for that.

Risks you must understand

Only invest money you won’t need for many years – and can afford to lose.
1 You could lose money Private companies can fail or be sold for less than you paid. You could lose some or all of it.
2 Your money is locked in There is no easy way to sell before an IPO or sale – and the company may never list.
3 You own units, not shares The SPV holds the shares for you. You rely on the SPV and the company’s transfer rules.
4 Less information Private companies share far less than listed ones. New funding rounds can also shrink your stake.
5 Currency and tax You invest in US dollars, so rupee or dirham moves change your return. US tax rules also apply.
StockifyFull list in each deal’s risk disclosure document

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell before the IPO?

Usually not. There is no public market for SPV units. Plan to hold until the company lists or is sold. If an early sale is possible, it may be at a lower price.

What if the company blocks the transfer?

Many private companies must approve share sales. If a company blocks the transfer, the deal doesn’t go ahead and escrow returns your money. For Helix AI, approval is already received.

What do I actually own?

Units in a Delaware SPV set up for that one deal. The SPV owns the company’s shares, and your units are your slice of them.

What happens at IPO?

The shares are usually locked up for 180 days. After that, the SPV sells them and pays you, or moves the shares to your own brokerage account.

Are my documents available?

Yes. The PPM, subscription agreement, SPV operating agreement and risk disclosure open once your eligibility is checked. Statements are sent by email.

What does it cost?

3.5% one-time when you invest (3.0% placement + 0.5% SPV set-up & admin), no yearly fee, and 10% of any profit at exit.
